conviction_note: Evidence is two-sided: the quarter (Jul-Sep, before SpaceX's Oct 8 spectrum deal) is likely to land on a bar the CEO set publicly on Sep 9, and the stock has a 7-of-7 positive print history with calls bid. Against that, AT&T beat and raised on Oct 21 and still fell about 5% on Starlink fear, and the narrative overhang (SpaceX 800 MHz spectrum, talks over 80k cell sites) is what has moved VZ 18% off its high. So abs_move 4.0 (straddle 4.75% over 7 days in a 43% realised-vol tape) and p_up 55 give +0.4. The findings sum to +0.15 and are not fitted to that.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus adj. EPS $1.28 / revenue $34.865bn / EBITDA $13.77bn (Hudson Labs, https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/verizon-q3-2026-earnings-preview-vz-guidance-estimates-key, 2026-10-06). TIKR gives ~$1.28 / ~$34.9bn (https://www.tikr.com/blog/verizon-slides-as-spacexs-8-billion-spectrum-deal-clouds-wireless-pricing). CoinCentral gives EPS ~$1.27. So two sources agree within a cent. No sourced consensus exists for postpaid phone net adds. The operative subscriber bar is management's own: positive phone net accounts in Q3, and 2026 phone net adds at the 'top end' of 750k-1M, which implies ~761k in H2 against 239k in H1. FY26 guide: adj. EPS $4.99-5.04, FCF $21.9-22.1bn, buybacks up to $4.5bn, M&B service revenue +2.5-3.0%.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 83.4M shares (~2% of float), 3.0 days to cover (ShortSqueeze, 2026-08-19, https://shortsqueeze.com/?symbol=VZ). That matches 85.7M / 2.44 days at the 2026-07-15 settlement (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/vz/short-interest/), with borrow at 0.3%. Not a crowded short. Baseline 25d skew is -4.67 vol points (calls over puts, 'upside paid'), put/call OI is 0.55, ATM IV is 42.6%, and the 7-day straddle is 4.75%. Event-implied move reads 0 only because 20d realised vol is 42.9% after the Starlink selloff. On Oct 23 put volume rose: P/C 1.11 vs 0.69 typical, 30d IV 28.75 (GuruFocus, https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9140159/verizon-vz-stock-dips-amid-rising-put-options-and-elevated-volatility-on-october-23-2026). Tape: -5.35% over 20d, -13.4% from the 52w high, and -17.8% Sep 15-Oct 9 including a -10.1% day on Oct 9 (ex-div $0.71 included). VZ's own print reactions are 7 of 7 up, median 2.26%, max 11.83%.

findings.finding: On Sep 9 (Goldman Sachs conference, two-thirds through Q3) CEO Schulman said Q3 'will be positive phone net accounts' for the first time in at least 3 years, and that 2026 postpaid phone net adds will be at the 'top end' of the 750k-1M guide. The top end implies ~761k in H2, roughly 380k a quarter, against 184k in Q2. The Q3 phone-add number is therefore pre-signalled high and is the main subscriber line the print is judged on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Subscriber beats have been bought. Jan 30 2026 (Q4 2025, highest net adds since 2019, 2026 guide) +11.83%. Jul 24 2026 (184k, best in 5 yrs, guide raised) +5.84%. Apr 27 2026 (55k, first positive Q1 since 2013) +1.55%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and so sets the bar, not a surprise. What is not priced is whether he delivered: since he spoke, the stock fell ~18% on a sector-wide Starlink re-rating, not on any Q3 subscriber datum. Had the market doubted the Q3 commitment, you would expect VZ to underperform T and TMUS on the SpaceX days. It did not: Oct 9 intraday VZ -10.9% vs T -11.3% and TMUS -12.8%. Inside guidance, so sized small.
findings.independence: The guidance range itself comes from a different document, Hudson Labs' preview (https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/verizon-q3-2026-earnings-preview-vz-guidance-estimates-key). The Q3 statement has one source (the CEO's remarks via TIKR).

findings.finding: Peer AT&T reported Oct 21: adj. EPS $0.65 vs $0.60 consensus, revenue $32.3bn vs ~$31.7bn, 2026 EPS guide raised to 'the $2.40 range'. It still fell ~5% pre-market and ~3% on the day, on SpaceX/Starlink Mobile fear and phone adds slowing (379k vs 432k in Q2, roughly in line). Two days later (Oct 23) VZ fell 3.2% on a Bloomberg report that SpaceX is negotiating access to ~80,000 US cell sites. That sector reaction function means a clean VZ beat may not be paid, and the call is management's first chance to answer SpaceX's Oct 8 800 MHz spectrum purchase.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior VZ print under a Starlink overhang. The closest read is AT&T's Oct 21 print (beat and raise, sold). TIKR says this is AT&T's second post-beat drop this year. VZ itself has risen on 7 of 7 prints.
findings.why_not_priced: The SpaceX overhang is clearly in the price: NTM P/E 8.2x on Oct 9 vs 9.0x on Sep 30, and Bernstein/KeyBanc targets cut to $44. What may not be priced is the reaction function. The skew is still call-bid (-4.67) and VZ has risen on 7 of 7 prints, so the options market is leaning toward VZ being paid for a beat. AT&T's print says the sector is not being paid. Sign kept against the skew because the counterparty's print is the newest direct evidence of how this tape treats beats; size kept small because short interest is low and positioning is not crowded.
findings.independence: The Oct 23 SpaceX/80k-cell-site report and VZ -3.2% come from a different source (https://coincentral.com/verizon-vz-stock-slides-after-report-spacex-seeks-80000-cell-sites, https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/23/telecom-stocks-fall-as-spacex-eyes-80000-cell-sites-t-mobile-sinks-5-att-drops-4-verizon-slides-3/). The Oct 8 deal and Oct 9 drop come from TIKR (https://www.tikr.com/blog/verizon-stock-fell-10-in-a-day-after-spacexs-spectrum-deal-heres-what-its-ceo-said-about-starlink-in-september).

findings.finding: Q3 switching pool read-across, both from counterparties that spoke after Verizon's last statement. T-Mobile guided Q3 postpaid account net adds to only ~250k, with deliberately elevated account churn from a rate-plan modernization concentrated in small-line accounts. AT&T's Q3 postpaid phone churn rose to 0.92% from 0.86%, and its phone adds slowed to 379k from 432k with promotional discounts noted. Two rivals shedding or slowing in Q3 is consistent with Verizon taking a larger share of switchers. AT&T's 8-K shows 379k phone adds and 0.92% churn.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Jul 2026 phone-add beat (184k) with lower churn (0.84%) was bought +5.84%.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews (Hudson Labs Oct 6, TIKR) anchor on Q2's 184k and carry no phone-add consensus at all, so the read-across from AT&T's slowdown and T-Mobile's guided churn spike has no number on the street to move. If it were priced, VZ would have outperformed T after AT&T's print. Instead it fell 2-3% with it on Oct 21. This is a proxy: Verizon has not confirmed where the switchers went, and cable MVNOs are the other candidate. Hence small.
findings.independence: T-Mobile's guided Q3 churn spike comes from a different document (https://finviz.com/news/405192/t-mobiles-planned-churn-spike-puts-a-bruised-stocks-growth-story-to-the-test, 2026-10-20).

findings.finding: The YipitData card panel (published 2026-08-21) shows Verizon's switcher deficit against T-Mobile widening in May-July 2026. Verizon had 2.4 outflows to T-Mobile per reverse inflow (968 vs 408), and its outflow rate rose from 32.4 to 38.8 per 10k base customers, while flows with AT&T were near even. July is the first month of Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no history on third-party switching data. Verizon's own Q2 report (overlapping May-June) showed 184k phone adds and churn down 6bps YoY, and the stock rose +5.84%. The broader company number contradicted this panel for the overlapping months.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a niche panel product not carried on the wire. But it is a narrow proxy: the merchant label blends wireless and Fios, and it is panel counts, not share. It is already contradicted in size by Verizon's own Q2 report for the overlapping May-June months, so it is sized below that series.
findings.independence: None points the same way. Verizon's Q2 results (https://www.verizon.com/about/news/verizon-delivers-record-2q26-results) point the other way.

findings.finding: Verizon raised FY26 guidance twice this year: in Q2, FCF to $21.9-22.1bn from $21.5bn+, adj. EPS to $4.99-5.04 from $4.95-4.99, and buybacks to up to $4.5bn from $3.0bn+, with $3.5bn done in H1. With the stock at ~8x NTM EPS and a ~13.8% NTM FCF yield after the SpaceX selloff, a third raise or faster buybacks is the lever available on the print. Peer AT&T raised its EPS guide on Oct 21.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance moves have been the biggest VZ print reactions. Jan 30 2026 first 2026 guide +11.83%. Jul 24 2026 second raise and buyback raise +5.84%. Apr 27 2026 EPS guide raise +1.55%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS of $1.28 and 'guidance raised twice' are in every preview, so a reaffirmation is priced. A third raise or a buyback step-up at an 8x multiple is not: TIKR shows NTM EPS estimates slipping ($5.09 to $5.07) rather than rising into the print. This is inference, not a company signal, so it sits mid-small. The downside of the range covers a hold, or FCF guidance trimmed for Frontier integration.
findings.independence: TIKR valuation and estimate drift (https://www.tikr.com/blog/verizon-stock-fell-10-in-a-day-after-spacexs-spectrum-deal-heres-what-its-ceo-said-about-starlink-in-september). AT&T's raised EPS guide (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000732717/000073271726000370/t-3q2026exhibit991.htm) is a peer, not this company.

findings.finding: Revenue line risk. Q2 revenue was $34.25bn vs ~$35.16bn consensus, with equipment revenue -19.7% YoY on lower upgrade rates and no subsidies. The Q3 consensus of $34.865bn implies +1.8% QoQ, while management said in Sep 'you're not going to see phones on us even with new launches' (iPhone 18 cycle). Another equipment-led revenue miss is plausible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue missed by ~$0.9bn and the stock rose +5.84%. This name does not trade on headline revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: The headline revenue consensus has stayed above the run-rate implied by Verizon's no-subsidy stance, but the market looked through exactly this miss last quarter. Near zero.
findings.independence: The Q2 revenue miss vs $35.16bn comes from a different source (https://coincentral.com/verizon-vz-stock-slides-after-report-spacex-seeks-80000-cell-sites).

findings.finding: Insiders have made 10 open-market sales and 0 purchases in 6 months, including EVP & CHRO Samantha Hammock selling 73,069 shares (~$3.5m) and Kyle Malady (Verizon Business CEO) selling 1,100 shares at $44.48 on Oct 20 under a 10b5-1 plan.
findings.why_not_priced: These are small, mostly pre-arranged sales. They carry little information and are filed for completeness.
findings.independence: The Oct 20 Malady sale is in a different source (https://coincentral.com/verizon-vz-stock-slides-after-report-spacex-seeks-80000-cell-sites).

findings.finding: Hurricane Isaias hit the Gulf Coast around Oct 8-10, 2026. Some sites were out of service, there were multiple fiber cuts on the Central Gulf Coast, and service was fully restored Oct 13-14. Verizon is giving affected postpaid/SMB customers free unlimited service through Oct 31. This is a Q4 cost item that may be mentioned in the Q4 outlook.
findings.why_not_priced: It is too small to matter on a $138bn-revenue company and does not touch Q3. Filed so a judge can see it.

outside_window.finding: FCC approval of SpaceX's purchase of Grain Management's 800 MHz spectrum. Evercore sees full 5G-quality Starlink Mobile service possible from 1H 2028; it is a multi-year competitive question, not resolvable on the print.
T-Mobile's Q3 print on Oct 28 (after the exit window) will show whether its guided churn spike fed Verizon.

baseline_tension: The skew (calls bid, -4.67) and the 7-of-7 positive print history argue up. The 20-day slide is a sector re-rating on SpaceX, not a Q3 datum. The newest counterparty evidence (AT&T sold its beat and raise) cuts against the skew, so p_up sits only modestly above 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (inside guidance): the CEO's Q3 net-accounts/top-end commitment lands inside what the company told the market, so +0.5 became +0.3.
Lesson 7 (skew/short interest): the Starlink/AT&T reaction-function negative runs against a call-bid skew with a non-crowded short, so -1.0 became -0.8, with the reason stated in why_not_priced.
Lesson 5 (narrow proxy vs broad series): YipitData's panel is contradicted in size by Verizon's own Q2 report for the overlapping months, so -0.5 became -0.3.
Lesson 1 (reaction function): the revenue-miss finding was cut from -0.3 to -0.1 because this name rose +5.84% on a ~$0.9bn revenue miss in Q2.
Lesson 2 (one-off): the hurricane relief cost is a Q4 one-off with no path to guidance; -0.1 became -0.05.
Left standing: the guidance-raise finding (+0.7, the line VZ has paid on), the counterparty switching read-across (+0.5), insider sales (-0.1), abs_move 4.0 and p_up 55.
